teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji assistant coaches still unannounced after his appointment this week
teams.body: Latest reporting still has no official announcement of an assistant coaching staff under Jake White, who was appointed earlier this week and named his first 28-man squad for the Centennial Test against Japan, according to Planet Rugby. SA Rugby Magazine has reported that White is turning to a trusted Springbok ally, but no name has been confirmed by Fiji Rugby. The question stays open until the union officially names the staff.

teams.heading: England's former lock David Ribbans becomes Springbok-eligible on 27 October
teams.body: Former England lock David Ribbans, 11 caps for England, completes his three-year international stand-down on 27 October, opening the door to a Springbok call-up. Erasmus has said South Africa are 'looking at someone like David Ribbans', though the 31-year-old Toulon forward has previously made clear he would not take a switch lightly. He has spoken of England becoming his second home and said switching 'wouldn't be right towards England'. Eligibility, in other words, does not settle the matter.

lead.why: It is the only new men's story on the shortlist with a clear England angle, and the other new item is a women's match already covered today.

teams.heading: France winger Bielle-Biarrey stranded at Bristol Airport with Bordeaux Bègles teammates
teams.body: France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey was one of four Bordeaux Bègles players temporarily denied entry to the UK, stranded at Bristol Airport with loose forward Romain Gardrat, loosehead Matis Perchaud and Tonga prop Toma Taufa, plus a fitness coach. A club source told AFP the group lacked valid Electronic Travel Authorisation permits, their approvals linked to passports renewed earlier this year. The issue was resolved through the French embassy in London, and the players rejoined the squad before Bordeaux's Champions Cup opener against Gloucester.

lead.why: A France international stranded at Bristol Airport is a story fans would text each other, and it is the most France-specific item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Ireland women's Aoife Wafer ruled out of South Africa Tests through injury
teams.body: Ireland women's Aoife Wafer was ruled out of Ireland's South Africa Tests by injury, and BBC Rugby Union also reported her out of the Japan game in the WXV Global Series. The latest reporting on this dates from late September, and no later update has been reported, so her return remains unconfirmed. Until Ireland name her again, the last known position is that she is out.

teams.heading: Italy face South Africa next, after their 32-14 home defeat last November
teams.body: Italy's next fixture is Round 4 against South Africa, who beat them 32-14 at home in November 2025 in an International Friendly. That result stands as their most recent meeting. In the log, Italy sit 11 of 12 after three matches, still without a win, having scored 37 points and conceded 131 across those three matches.

teams.heading: Scotland women face the Wallaroos again in Canberra after Sydney rout
teams.body: Scotland women face the Wallaroos again on Friday in Canberra, after an eight-try 56-12 defeat in Sydney on Saturday. Katie Buchanan gave them a fifth-minute lead and captain Rachel Malcolm also crossed, but Australia scored five tries before half-time and Desiree Miller became the first Wallaroo to reach 20 Test tries. Caretaker coach Dave Butcher also had to replace Sarah Bonar, lost to illness shortly before kick-off, with Hollie Cunningham.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item that moves the women's story forward, with the Canberra rematch on Friday as a new fact.

teams.heading: Dafydd Jenkins says Welsh players moving to Prem can strengthen regions
teams.body: Dafydd Jenkins believes the flood of Welsh talent heading to the English Prem will benefit the home game. The Exeter lock, 23, who has spent all his senior career at Sandy Park, says the move opens space for the next generation. "I think the positive in that is that they're opening up space for another young hooker, another young back-rower," he told BBC Sport. Captain Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake joined Gloucester from the Ospreys this summer, and Jenkins has started all three of Exeter's league matches this season.

lead.why: It is a men's Wales story not yet in the edition archive, and it is about the national side's players rather than a bystander piece.

teams.heading: Argentina's 2035 World Cup bid still awaits World Rugby's decision
teams.body: Argentina's bid to stage the 2035 Rugby World Cup remains open. The Pumas lead a joint four-nation South American candidacy with Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, first presented in early October, and the decision rests with World Rugby, which has not yet named a host. Planet Rugby says the bid will challenge World Rugby's desire for a European return, while South Africa is billed as a dark horse. No outcome has been reported as of today.

teams.heading: Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i looked lost in defence as All Blacks exploited him
teams.body: Planet Rugby's ratings of Saturday's second Bledisloe Test, a 43-21 defeat in Sydney, singled out Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i for particular criticism. The former league man looked lost in defence, was often caught out of position and missed five tackles, and the All Blacks exploited him on multiple occasions. His early offload set up a Wallabies breakaway, but he struggled from there. His midfield partner Isaac Henry also looked unsure defensively, leaving gaps the All Blacks targeted.

teams.heading: Japan's 63-14 win over USA is their biggest in last 11 games
teams.body: Japan have scored 309 points and conceded 308 across their last 11 games, averages of 28.1 scored and 28 conceded per match. The biggest win in that window came in September, when Japan beat USA 63-14 at home in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. Their most recent result was a 15-42 defeat to France in Round 3. Their next match is Wales in Round 4 of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: All Blacks beat Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney for 13th straight win
teams.body: The All Blacks scored seven tries to the Wallabies' three in Sydney, winning 43-21 for a 13th straight win over Australia. Beauden Barrett scored a brace and Josh Moorby also crossed twice, and the result followed a 50-19 win at Eden Park that retained the Bledisloe Cup. Dave Rennie's side now sit second in the World Rugby rankings, 0.82 rating points behind South Africa.

lead.why: It is a new men's Test result that the other shortlist items do not offer: the Bledisloe win and the 13th straight over Australia, not a repeat of the TMO or Tupou Vaa'i stories already on this tab.

teams.heading: Cheswill Jooste scores hat-trick as Bulls beat Stade Français 56-20
teams.body: Bulls wing Cheswill Jooste, 20, scored a hat-trick as the Bulls opened their Investec Champions Cup campaign with a 56-20 win over Stade Français in hot conditions on Saturday. His first came barely half a minute in, after he raced onto a Harold Vorster kick, and his third was a walk-in in the 73rd minute. Planet Rugby's takeaways describe him as a hot Springboks prospect, with Sebastian de Klerk giving the Bulls a second electric wing.

lead.why: A new story about a 20-year-old Springboks prospect scoring a hat-trick, which is more talked-about than the rankings or older background pieces.
